summary: Iteration 8 — backend-only verification of the multi-project reports + address per project + touch-ups flag + backward-compat + GET /customers/history. Wrote 15 pytest cases in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration8_multiproject.py, ALL 15 PASSING in 48.26s (-n 0). Coverage: (1) POST /api/visits accepts new optional project_id — round-trips through /visits/today; visit without project_id still succeeds and serializes project_id as null. (2) POST /api/reports with 2 projects — all fields (customer_name, address, notes, materials_used, start_time, end_time, priority_flag, touch_up) persist and are returned on the response; AI summary body contains project markers (customer names and address). (3) Backward-compat: created a legacy-style report (no projects field) after seeding two visits with distinct project_ids — GET /api/reports/{id} returns non-empty projects derived from those visits via _derive_projects_from_visits (one entry per unique project_id). (4) GET /api/customers/history — happy path returns customer + 2 visits + >=1 report (seeded id present) + photos + counts matching; case-insensitive partial substring match works; empty name → 400; missing Bearer → 401. Route ordering confirmed: GET /customers/history is not shadowed by DELETE /customers/{customer_id}. (5) Touch-Ups flag {'type':'Touch-Ups','reason':...} persists in priority_flags, and the AI summary body contains 'TOUCH-UP' (case-insensitive) — the system prompt now instructs GPT to add '[TOUCH-UP: <address>]' bullets. (6) Regression: GET /api/reports returns 200 with every doc carrying a `projects` list (legacy docs are back-filled on read); POST /api/reports/{id}/tts returns 200 with audio_data_url + voice_provider (openai as expected — ElevenLabs quota still exhausted); POST /api/reports/{id}/regenerate-summary returns 200 and preserves the 2-project structure; GET /api/customers unchanged. No frontend testing this iteration per E1 request.

minor.issue: Response is not wrapped in a Pydantic response_model — customer/visits/reports use raw dicts. Works today but any Mongo `_id` leak would break clients. Currently safe because the endpoint uses {'_id': 0} projection on all three finds; adding an explicit response_model would future-proof it.

reports_summary is only a subset of fields (id, report_date, author_name, author_role, priority_level, created_at). If the frontend later needs `projects` or `photos` from those reports to render the pin drop pop-up, the client would need a second GET /reports/{id}. Consider embedding projects[] filtered to the matching customer, or expose a photos-per-report list.

photos list only pulls from visits; report-level project photos (projects[].photos) are ignored. If a project block is added directly with photos and no linked visit, those photos won't appear in the history photos array. Low-priority since visit photos are the main upload path today.

When the user supplies `projects` explicitly, the server does NOT link any of today's actual visits into those project entries — visit_ids remains []. Losing the visit↔project link means the customer_history 'pin tap → visit detail' flow relies solely on customer_name substring match, which is fragile if two customers share a first name. Consider auto-attaching visits whose project_id matches an entry in projects[] or whose customer_name matches.

There is no server-side validation that project_id refers to an actual ProjectEntry inside today's report. Front-end must handle the 'add to which project?' UX flow — backend accepts any string. If a project_id is a stale/typo value, the visit is silently orphaned. Consider adding a lightweight check or exposing GET /projects/today to enumerate valid IDs.

action_items: No blocking issues — multi-project reports, address-per-project, touch-ups flag, /customers/history, and backward-compat are all working as specified.

(Optional) Auto-link today's visits to matching projects at POST /reports time (match on project_id or customer_name+address) so `projects[].visit_ids` is populated and the mobile 'pin tap → visit detail' flow can navigate without a client-side join.

(Optional) Add explicit Pydantic response_model to GET /customers/history and expand `reports` entries with the project block(s) matching the queried customer so the client can render the pop-up without a second round trip.

(Optional) Include project-level photos (projects[].photos) in the /customers/history photos array so pin-drop pop-ups show photos for report-only projects (i.e., projects added without a linked visit).
(Carry-over from iteration 7) server.py is now 1894 lines — split into routers when convenient.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:762-799 (_derive_projects_from_visits) — when the same project_id appears in later visits, only `notes` and `photos` are merged; start_time/end_time keep the FIRST visit's timestamps and are never widened to (min start, max end). Cosmetic today, but the customer_history UI will show only the first visit's time window.

server.py:848-854 — user-supplied `projects` are trusted verbatim as authoritative; a client bug that sends an empty projects list PLUS include_visits=True currently drops back to derived-from-visits. That's fine, but the code path is ambiguous — an empty explicit list vs missing field looks identical after `data.projects or []`. Consider distinguishing via a sentinel or requiring `projects: Optional[List[...]] = None`.

server.py:1183-1242 (customer_history) — the $or query on {visits.customer_name} and {projects.customer_name} does not use an index; on large collections this will scan every report. Add a compound index on visits.customer_name / projects.customer_name (mongo supports multikey indexes on array fields).

server.py:1191 — re.escape prevents regex injection which is good, but there's no upper bound on name length. A 5MB `name=…` query param would create a huge compiled regex. Consider capping name to e.g. 200 chars.

server.py:667-676 (build_ai_summary) — priority_flags iteration relies on f.get('type'); if the frontend sends {'type': None, 'reason': 'foo'} the prompt line becomes '- None — reason: foo'. Minor defensive-coding opportunity.

rca_of_issue: N/A — this iteration validates new features (multi-project reports, address per project, touch-ups flag, /customers/history endpoint, backward-compat auto-migration). All 15 test cases pass on first run; no bugs to root-cause. Implementation notes: ProjectEntry (server.py:167-183) is a full Pydantic model with a UUID default for id; ReportCreate.projects is List[ProjectEntry] with default_factory=list, so old clients that omit the field still work. Backward compat is enforced in three places: POST /reports (server.py:848-854 falls back to _derive_projects_from_visits when projects is empty), GET /reports (server.py:1046-1048 back-fills on read for legacy docs), and GET /reports/{id} (server.py:1060-1061). _derive_projects_from_visits (server.py:762-799) groups by project_id when set — merging visit_ids, photos, and appending notes — else emits one project per visit. The AI-summary prompt (server.py:640-665) contains explicit instructions to group WORK COMPLETED by project and to emit '[TOUCH-UP: <address>]' bullets, which GPT respected in all test runs.
